newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PZB starts new ferry line to Sweden June 1.
newsitem.headline: Polish PZB starts new ferry line to Sweden June 1.

text.p: Polska Zegluga Baltycka (PZB) will open a new route between Poland and Nyanshamn in Sweden from June 1, the Polish Baltic shipping line said in a statement.
"Starting from June 1, PZB is opening a new line to Nyanashamn...which will be served by a ferry daily except on Tuesdays," the statement issued late on Monday said.
PZB has now five ferries. In June a new one, an Australian-built catamaran, will operate between Poland's Swinoujscie and Malmoe. @
The journey time of the vessel which can carry 700 people, will be four hours instead of the previous seven.
In 1996 PZB carried 386,000 passengers and 75,000 cars compared with 429,000 passengers and 90,000 cars in 1995.
It expects a 15 percent rise this year in the number of passengers carried and of 10 percent in the number of cars.
In 1996 the company had revenue of 141.7 million zlotys after 138.8 million in 1995 and showed a net loss of 9.2 million zlotys against a 1.9 million loss in 1995. @
Costs including investment in 1996 were 150.1 million zlotys against 137.7 million in 1995.
